picks.title: #12901 How Can the Eucharist Be Jesus Body? Faith and Rituals - William Albrecht
picks.summary:
“How can the Eucharist be Jesus’ body?” This question opens a discussion on the profound mystery of the Eucharist, addressing concerns about Jesus’ words on spirit and flesh. The conversation also touches on the historical context of the Eucharist, the nature of Catholic Mass compared to other rituals, and how to respond to misconceptions from friends of different faiths.

picks.showTitle: The Catechism in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)
picks.title: Day 259: The New Commandment (2026)
picks.summary:
We continue our examination of the New Law or Law of the Gospel, specifically the Golden Rule and New Commandment of Jesus. Fr. Mike emphasizes that the New Commandment requires us to love God as the center of everything we are and everything we have. He also unpacks how the New Commandment is also known as the law of love, grace, and freedom. Today’s readings are Catechism paragraphs 1970-1974.

This episode has been found to be in conformity with the Catechism by the Institute on the Catechism, under the Subcommittee on the Catechism, USCCB.

For the complete reading plan, visit ascensionpre
picks.reason: Explains the New Commandment of love as central to Christian moral life.

picks.showTitle: Sunday Homilies with Fr. Mike Schmitz
picks.title: 09/20/26 Blind Spots: Entitlement
picks.summary: Homily from the Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time. God does not owe me anything. Entitlement does not always look like entitlement. Sometimes, it simply feels like getting what we deserve. Whether it comes from pride or pain, we can believe that we are owed more. But grace is, by definition, an undeserved gift. The cure for entitlement is to stop asking what we are owed and to start asking what God has entrusted to us...and then receive it with gratitude. Mass Readings from September 20, 2026: Isaiah 55:6-9 Psalm 145:2-3, 8-9, 17-18Philippians 1:20c-24, 27a Matthew 20:1-16a]]>
picks.reason: A homily reflecting on entitlement and grace from a Catholic Sunday Mass.

picks.title: The Woman of Canossa Castle
picks.summary: In 1077, the King of Germany and future Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV walked barefoot in the snow and waited three days outside of Canossa Castle. He had been excommunicated by the Pope and was hoping to appeal to the Pope's sense of forgiveness. But the Pope was only at Canossa Castle himself because he was being hosted by Matilda of Tuscany, a fascinating figure at the heart of one of the most famous religious episodes in history.
